title: Freya and the Uniform
premise: Coral Dravenmoor, a mapmaker's apprentice in the coastal city of Vellmark, has spent two years finishing the grand atlas her master died for — only to have the war bureau seize it for military use. When a wounded stranger arrives bearing her master's unmistakable handwriting on orders dated after his death, Coral discovers the atlas contains a hidden cipher proving the bureau falsified the border maps that started the war. Torn between loyalty to the bureau officer she loves and the truth her master bled for, she smuggles the corrected maps across the lines to deliver the promise she made in peacetime to her master's son — now declared an enemy officer. The century turns with the truth published, the atlas burned by the bureau but remembered in hand-copied form, and Coral choosing exile and love over the city that demanded her silence.
about_author: Lena Thornbury is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border maps before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the people who draw lines on paper and the people who die because of them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the winter of 1898, Coral inks the final plate of Master Aldous Vey's atlas in their cluttered workshop, remembering his death two years prior and the promise she made to finish his life's work. Emotional beat: devotion shadowed by grief, and the quiet pride of a craft nearly complete.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The war bureau arrives with sealed orders and confiscates the atlas plates 'for the duration,' leaving Coral with proofs only. Lieutenant Casper Ilyen, the bureau's young cartographic officer and Coral's old friend, is visibly uncomfortable but dutiful. Emotional beat: the first intrusion of the state into the sanctum of her work.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tide Gate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A half-frozen stranger, Rell, collapses at the workshop door clutching dispatch papers bearing Master Vey's handwriting — dated eight months after his death. Coral hides him from a patrol, torn between fear and the impossible evidence in her hands. Emotional beat: shock curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Examining the dispatch, Coral confirms the hand is Vey's — and recognizes the marginal cipher he taught her, encoding corrections to the border maps. Rell claims Vey survived his reported death and was working against the bureau. Emotional beat: the ground of her grief shifting beneath her.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a flashback in Vey's voice via a recovered letter. She compares Rell's cipher to her retained proofs and finds the bureau has redrawn the Kelvern Pass border — the falsification that justified the war. Emotional beat: horror at the precision of the lie.

chapters.title: Casper's Uniform
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper audits the workshop's seized materials, suspects Coral knows more than she says, and covers for her with his superior, Colonel Brase. He recalls their peacetime friendship and his quiet love for her. Emotional beat: duty and affection beginning to grind against each other.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback to 1895. Vey's son Tam, a junior surveyor then, made Coral swear that if anything happened to his father, she'd carry the true maps to him 'wherever the lines fall.' Tam now serves the enemy state across the strait. Emotional beat: the weight of a promise made when borders seemed permanent.

chapters.title: Rell's Confession
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell admits he was Vey's courier in hiding, that Vey was murdered by bureau agents when the falsification was discovered, and that the cipher's key was split between the dispatch and the atlas proofs Coral kept. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt and a courier's stubborn faith in Coral.

chapters.title: Colonel Brase's Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Brase invites Coral to 'advise' the bureau on the atlas, flattering her while probing what proofs survived. She performs loyalty, lying smoothly for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: the intoxicating and frightening discovery that she can deceive.

chapters.title: The Split Key
chapters.summary: Coral and Rell's alternating POV. Working by lamplight, they combine cipher and proofs to reconstruct Vey's corrected map of Kelvern Pass. Rell argues it must reach Tam's command; Coral resists aiding the enemy. Emotional beat: truth becoming a burden with a price attached.

chapters.title: What Casper Saw
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper discovers Rell's hiding place but says nothing, instead warning Coral obliquely that Brase has ordered her workshop watched. His silence is his first act of treason. Emotional beat: love choosing itself over the uniform, tremblingly.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The bureau publicly burns 'subversive cartography,' including Vey's original field notebooks. Coral watches her master's life go up in smoke and understands there will be no safe way back. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Courier's Route
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell maps the smuggling route across the frozen strait, revealing his network is broken and he cannot carry the maps alone. Coral volunteers; he refuses to let her. Emotional beat: two frightened people arguing over who gets to be brave.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A junior clerk reports Rell's presence; Brase orders the workshop raided at dawn. Casper must decide whether to warn Coral, knowing discovery ends his career and possibly his life. Emotional beat: the point of no return approached in slow motion.

chapters.title: Flight from Vellmark
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Warned by Casper's note, Coral and Rell flee with the corrected maps sewn into her coat lining, pursued through the dock district. Casper delays the raid by an hour and is arrested for it. Emotional beat: escape purchased with someone else's sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Frozen Strait
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Crossing the ice at night, Rell is shot by a border patrol and dies in Coral's arms, making her swear to finish the delivery. She buries the maps' existence under her grief and walks on. Emotional beat: loss hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Enemy Lines
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Posing as a refugee mapmaker, Coral reaches the enemy garrison at Kelvern and requests Tam by name — and is detained as a suspected spy. Emotional beat: the terrible irony of keeping a promise to the wrong side of a line.

chapters.title: The Son of the Master
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam confronts Coral, bitter that his father chose maps over family, until he deciphers the corrected border and understands what Vey died protecting. He vouches for her with his command. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance colliding into fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Map Goes to War
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, with Coral present. The corrected map is presented to the enemy high command; instead of exploiting it, Tam argues for publishing it — exposing the falsification to both nations and forcing a ceasefire at Kelvern. Emotional beat: truth wielded as an instrument of peace, not victory.

chapters.title: Casper's Choice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Imprisoned, Casper is offered reinstatement if he denounces Coral. Instead he leaks the falsification evidence to a neutral journalist before his tribunal. Emotional beat: a man finally measuring himself against his own uniform and finding it too small.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On New Year's Eve 1899, the corrected map is published in neutral papers on both sides of the strait; the Kelvern ceasefire holds and an inquiry begins. Casper, released and stripped of rank, crosses the ice to find her. Emotional beat: the old century's lies ending with it.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue in spring 1900. In exile in the neutral free port of Halden, Coral opens a small mapshop with Tam and Casper, hand-copying the true atlas since the original plates are lost. She measures the world in what can be carried — and carries it forward. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
